Agent Instructions for RdistNN

Source: AGENTS.md

Read this file before modifying code. It is the canonical instruction file for LLM agents and automated coding assistants working in this repository.

Mandatory read order

Before making changes, read these files in order:

  1. markdown_notes/design/01_interface_standardization_decisions.md
  2. markdown_notes/design/02_code_design_principles.md
  3. markdown_notes/design/03_input_validation_contract.md
  4. markdown_notes/design/04_api_shapes_and_input_formats.md
  5. markdown_notes/design/05_error_messages_and_warnings.md
  6. markdown_notes/design/13_existing_codebase_standardization_plan.md

For package-engineering, lifecycle, compiled-code, documentation, or CI work, also read as relevant:

  • markdown_notes/design/06_namespace_and_dependency_policy.md
  • markdown_notes/design/07_lifecycle_and_deprecation_policy.md
  • markdown_notes/design/08_comments_and_function_docs.md
  • markdown_notes/design/09_testing_and_regression_policy.md
  • markdown_notes/design/10_rcpp_and_compiled_code_policy.md
  • markdown_notes/design/11_examples_vignettes_and_pkgdown_policy.md
  • markdown_notes/design/12_release_and_ci_policy.md

For tuning-grid work read markdown_notes/design/14_integrated_tuning_grid_reuse.md; for PLQR inference work read markdown_notes/design/15_plqr_variance_estimation_rationale.md.

Markdown note layout

  • markdown_notes/design/ is the canonical, ordered design-policy corpus.
  • markdown_notes/rdistnn_roadmap.md is the compact live roadmap; read it before starting new package work. The pre-public overhaul is implemented; the public notation page is implemented in vignettes/notation-and-conventions.Rmd. Consult the roadmap for remaining long-term framework and packaging work.
  • Completed or superseded implementation plans are archived with status headers under markdown_notes/archive/ (packets dated 2026-07-09 and 2026-07-11, including the implemented pre-public roadmap and the historical package audit note); treat them as provenance, not as live instructions — they largely predate the 2026-07-08 API renames.

Repository-wide non-negotiable rules

  • User-facing high-level estimators may accept either:
    • explicit matrices and vectors; or
    • data.frame inputs, including tibbles.
  • After validation and interface resolution, internal computation must proceed on canonical numeric matrices and vectors.
  • Do not add stopifnot() to exported functions or to helpers on user-facing paths.
  • Validation must happen early and produce actionable, argument-specific messages.
  • Diagnostics should use clean user-facing stop() / warning() messages, generally with call. = FALSE.
  • Unknown return values must be handled consistently across wrappers.
  • Do not hand-edit generated files such as NAMESPACE or RcppExports.*.
  • New compiled paths must include fallback-equivalence tests.
  • New user-visible validation or behavior changes must include tests.
  • Do not introduce new interface conventions without updating the design notes.
  • Mathematica / Wolfram Language is available through wolframscript. Use it when helpful for symbolic derivations, finite combinatorial checks, or estimator-formula sanity checks, and record any substantive conclusions back into code, tests, or design notes.

Local CLI Tooling

Resolve tools in the environment actually running the command. In WSL, use command -v TOOL; in Windows PowerShell, use Get-Command TOOL. A tool installed on one machine is not evidence that it is on another machine’s PATH.

  • Use rg for source search; jq or Python for structured metadata.
  • Source installation needs a C++17 toolchain and Rcpp; use the platform requirements in README.md. Regenerate README.md from README.Rmd with devtools::build_readme() when its source changes.
  • Use Rscript for R work, actionlint for workflows, and wolframscript when a mathematical check calls for it. Follow the task-specific checks below.
  • Poppler (pdfinfo, pdftotext, pdftoppm) and qpdf support document inspection. Windows Ghostscript is commonly gswin64c; use magick for ImageMagick. Check availability before promising a build or check.
  • For Literature documents, use the shared catalog/extraction workflow below; do not replace its preserved evidence with ad hoc or in-place OCR.

Working rules for agents

When editing existing code:

  1. Prefer standardizing toward the design notes over local convenience.
  2. Preserve the public API unless there is a documented reason to change it.
  3. Keep the matrix/data.frame dual-interface policy at the outer boundary only.
  4. Reuse or extend shared validators instead of duplicating validation logic.
  5. Keep error messages specific about what was expected, what was received, and what the user should do instead when helpful.
  6. If a code path changes user-visible behavior, update tests and docs in the same pass.

In case of conflict

If code, comments, and design notes conflict, treat the numbered design notes as current source of truth unless there is a stronger repository-level instruction added after this file.

Literature and source lookup

For local literature work, use literature-vault; use obsidian-paper-notes for Obsidian paper/book notes. If a skill is not exposed, read its maintained SKILL.md under the vault’s _ai/skills/. Read the vault’s AGENTS.md and _ai/AGENTS.md before source or citation work.

The WSL vault is /home/jakob/research/Literature; Windows uses D:\Jakob_Clouds\Dropbox\Literature on the desktop and C:\Users\jakob\Dropbox\Literature on the laptop. Preserve both Windows layouts and resolve the current machine’s paths. Project-local 01_Literature collections and extraction caches are separate from this full vault.

Use the vault’s _bibliography/scripts/registry.py by absolute path: search for passages, search --find for discovery, and lookup for citation identity. Preserve existing project keys and unresolved identities. Check status’s catalog_schema_version and variants DOCUMENT_SHA: baseline-only catalogs use original sidecars plus supplemental MinerU reads; registered v5 catalogs support preferred read and --variant all --compare. Follow the vault’s _extractions/README.md and _bibliography/QUALITY.md for exact commands and review scope. Preferred text is not verification; inspect relied-on mathematics, tables, figures, and uncertain exact wording unless a current scoped visual review covers it. Keep extraction identities and physical/printed pages distinct. The personal vault is a research resource, not a repository build dependency.
